summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia and chronic tracheostomy was admitted for worsening odynophagia and dysphagia, two days after being unable to swallow without choking. She had recently completed a course of vancomycin for MRSA tracheitis, but symptoms recurred with thick, foul-smelling sputum from her trach. She remained afebrile with stable vital signs and no leukocytosis. Imaging showed no acute abnormalities in the chest or neck. ENT and GI evaluations found no structural or esophageal cause for dysphagia. She was treated symptomatically with pain management, dietary modifications, and anti-nausea medication. She gradually tolerated oral intake and was discharged home with instructions for ongoing symptom management, follow-up with GI and mental health providers, and reinforcement of trach and oral care.
